Maintenance Report — MNT-0048-001

Asset: WELL-0048 (SW-23 Well 048, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: flowline Work started: 02 Dec 2022 08:00 · Finished: 03 Dec 2022 06:00 · Well stopped for this job: 22 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0048-0007 on 2022-12-01 Report written: 04 Dec 2022

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0048-0007 at 09:45 on 2022-12-01 found crude oil on the pad: about 6.3% of the pad area, estimated 1.9 bbl. The inspector noted: "Pooled fluid near flowline." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 4.9 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Corrosion under a failed protective wrap on the coupling.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).
  • Hot work permit issued for welding; gas test before welding read 0% LEL, below the 10% limit (WS-04).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.
  2. Cut out the failed coupling and the pipe ends.
  3. Welded in new pipe and a new fitting.
  4. Coated the new joints.
  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Summary of the fix: replaced leaking flowline section and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 260 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 208 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.2 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0048-001; the manifest was only completed the following week (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.88% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0048-007

Asset: WELL-0048 (SW-23 Well 048, T200, Southwest Block 23) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 09 Sep 2023 08:00 · Finished: 17 Oct 2023 06:00 · Well stopped for this job: 910 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0048-0047 on 2023-09-07 Report written: 19 Oct 2023

What happened

Field staff reported that the pumper heard grinding from the walking beam and saw the horsehead wobbling. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0048-0047 showed the wellhead at 30.6 °C with the air at 29.9 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 36 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.

What happened

Field staff reported that the electric motor driving the pump jack had stopped and would not restart. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0048-0200 showed the wellhead at 39.6 °C with the air at 37.3 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
